findings.summary: The terminal-state assertion parses termination.state out of run.stdout.log, but the real producer never writes a tick-level termination JSON there, so the entry can never exit 0. run.stdout.log is the stdout of bin/deep-research-loop.sh, which emits only the loop-store put output, the '[deep-research-loop] mode=... run_root=...' line, and 'cat "$DRAIN_TMP"' — the loop-engine drain summary. The tick node's 'printf %s\n "$run_output"' (workflows/deep-research/tick/templates/tick.md:85) is captured by the engine into <run_dir>/journal.jsonl (that is exactly why scripts/check-drain-failures.mjs must open journal.jsonl to see per-tick results), and the drain summary is a single JSON object without a termination key — scripts/check-drain-failures.mjs:12 JSON.parse()s the entire drain stdout, and the repo's own real-machine records quote it as {"reason":"drained","rounds":1} (docs/dev-notes/dev_ledr_a10c_writebudget_01.md:43) and {"reason":"drained","rounds":0,"ticksByLabel":{"tick":0}} (docs/dev-notes/dev_ledr_a9_tick_trigger_01.md:12). Therefore scripts/e0-terminal-state.mjs exits 1 ('no termination JSON'), e0-verify.sh sets FAIL and exits 3, and bin/e0-regression.sh returns 3 even on a fully healthy run: criterion 8 / Z1 (runs to terminal state and exits 0) is unreachable by construction — the same 'entry can never reach a passing Z1' shape that got E0a and attempt 1 rejected, this time by reading a field from a stream that does not carry it.

The discriminating coverage for the terminal assertion is built on a hand-authored run.stdout.log that no real producer emits, which is the same fabricated-contract shape §1.3/§4 forbid. runVerify() synthesizes TERMINAL_LINE = {"channelId":"t","hasPendingWork":false,"termination":{...}} and writes it as run.stdout.log, so T-VERIFY-Z1/Z2/TERMINAL all validate a loop-output format that bin/deep-research-loop.sh never produces; no test drives bin/e0-verify.sh with stdout actually produced by the driver, and no test asserts that the driver's stdout contains a termination object. This is why the blocker above is invisible to a green suite, and it is precisely the discipline the spec extends to termination.state extraction in §1.2 and warns the reviewer about in §4 ('每一处从 HTTP 响应里取字段的代码，取的字段在真实 API 里到底存不存在').

e0-seed decides emptiness against the bus given by its baseUrl/tokenPath arguments, but publishes through bin/tick-entry.sh --seed, which resolves the bus from the inherited AGENT_BUS_URL / AGENT_BUS_TOKEN_FILE environment. bin/e0-regression.sh happens to keep the two consistent, so this is not a live defect, but any other caller whose argv and env diverge would check one board for emptiness and write append-only clues to another. Passing the resolved bus explicitly to the publish step would remove the coupling.
